campgrounds.reservations: By telephone to the park — 575-682-3375. Also listed on Hipcamp and RoverPass.
campgrounds.note: The only RV park inside the Village of Cloudcroft, 601 Columbine Boulevard, at about 8,400-9,000 ft, walking distance to the shops and the Trestle Recreation Area — the best of the options for a dog that wants a walk from the door. TWO THINGS TO SETTLE BY PHONE. (1) The operator publishes NO maximum RV length anywhere on its site; the Allstays directory lists 45 ft max, 16 sites, 4 pull-throughs, but that is third-party and must not be relied on for a 40 ft coach on a village street. (2) 30 AMP ONLY — no 50 amp service. For a 2005 40 ft coach that means one air conditioner at a time and careful load management; at 8,600 ft in late September you probably will not want air conditioning at all, so this may be a non-issue, but the electric heater and the microwave together will not be. Also: maximum 4 persons per site, and check-ins after dark are not permitted.

campgrounds.name: Silver Springs RV Park and Trout Pond
campgrounds.hookups: Full hookups — water, sewer, Wi-Fi, with 20, 30 and 50 amp service by site class. Clubhouse, community fire pit, stocked one-acre rainbow trout pond.

campgrounds.reservations: Online through the park's Premier Campground booking link from silverspringsrv.com, or by phone.
campgrounds.note: 449 NM-244, about 5 miles from Cloudcroft at nearly 9,000 ft — on the Ruidoso road, so the NM-244 drive starts at the gate. THE LENGTH IS UNPUBLISHED and the third-party figures disagree badly: RVshare, Outdoorsy and GoCampingAmerica all say 38 RV sites, all back-in, rigs to 45 ft; AllBiz says 42 spaces to 60 ft. Do not book on either number — phone. Two operator rules that matter for this rig: EVERY SITE IS BACK-IN (no pull-throughs, so the truck has to be unhooked before the site), and each site is limited to one RV and one vehicle with an additional charge for extras — the towed pickup will either be the one vehicle or will cost extra. Pets welcome on leash, not left unattended, $100 cleaning fee for waste left behind, no pets in the clubhouse. Office closed Wednesdays.

It is the only one of the three that is unambiguously a big-rig park: pull-throughs, 50 amp, gated, enclosed dog runs. BUT the operator publishes no maximum length either — AAA lists 32 sites, 80 ft max RV length, 16 pull-throughs, 50 full hookups, 20/30/50 amp; another directory lists pull-thrus at 32 x 83 ft. Confirm on the phone. Rates as published: standard $55 + tax nightly, deluxe covered $70, premium $85. ALTERNATIVE WORTH A CALL: Camp Rio (formerly Camp at Cloudcroft), 2180 Rio Penasco Road, Mayhill NM, 575-687-3715, camprionm.com — 6,500 ft, about 30 minutes east of Cloudcroft on the gentle side of US-82, full hookups with 30 and 50 amp, 50-amp PULL-THROUGHS, open year-round, pets on leash welcome. It publishes no maximum length either, but third-party listings describe 34 full-hookup sites with room for rigs to 75 ft. If Silver Springs turns out to be short, this is the next call.

elevation_note: Cloudcroft is 8,676 ft; the campgrounds on the mountain sit between about 8,400 and 9,000 ft. THE COACH: the problem is not sitting at altitude, it is getting there. US-82 from Alamogordo climbs about 4,300 ft in roughly 16-17 miles at a sustained ~6% grade with tight curves and New Mexico's only highway tunnel — RV forums are consistent that this is a hard pull up and a serious brake test down, and the tunnel's posted clearance is not something I could source, so it needs checking with NMDOT before committing a 13'6" coach. The gentle alternative is to arrive from the EAST on US-82 via Artesia and Mayhill, which is a long gradual climb rather than a wall; that also puts Camp Rio at Mayhill and 16 Springs on the way in. At 8,600 ft a naturally aspirated gas coach loses roughly 3% of power per 1,000 ft — about a quarter of its output — while a turbodiesel loses much less; either way plan the climb in low gear, watch coolant and transmission temperature, and descend on the engine brake rather than the service brakes. The generator will also derate and may need a jet/altitude adjustment for extended use, and propane appliances light less willingly. THE DOG: coming up from Alamogordo or the plains, the dog is gaining 4,000-5,000 ft in under an hour. Give it 24-48 hours before any long walk, keep water in front of it constantly, keep the first day's outings short and flat (the Trestle Recreation Area loop rather than the Osha rim), and watch for laboured breathing, unusual lethargy or refusal to eat — the same signs you would watch in yourself. Late September at 8,600 ft has a big diurnal swing and freezing nights are entirely possible, so the dog's bed comes inside and the water bowl does not stay out overnight; the same applies to the cat's water. The upside is real: this is one of the coolest places in the Southwest in September, and every trail listed here except White Sands is dog-legal on a leash.
